title: Asia stocks jump as Anthropic IPO filing revives AI trade
full_text:
Investing.com-- Asian shares rallied on Tuesday as technology stocks surged after artificial intelligence startup Anthropic filed for an initial public offering, lifting sentiment ahead of major corporate earnings and a series of central bank meetings later this week.
The rally followed a recovery on Wall Street on Monday, when the S&P 500 gained 0.7%, and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.8%, supported by renewed demand for AI-related shares.
U.S. stock index futures also edged higher in Asian trading Tuesday by 02:13 GMT.
Get premium stock market insights with InvestingPro subscription
KOSPI, Nikkei jump as tech shares track Anthropic IPO buzz
South Korea's tech-heavy KOSPI rose more than 4% in early trading, with heavyweights Samsung Electronics (KS:005930) and SK Hynix (KS:000660) climbing 5% and 7%, respectively.
South Korea's stronger-than-expected third-quarter GDP data provided further support for the region's technology rally. The economy grew 1.0% quarter-on-quarter, accelerating from 0.6% in the previous quarter and exceeding economists' expectations of 0.7%.
Japan's Nikkei 225 gained 2%, while the broader TOPIX index edged up 0.6%. Tokyo-listed SoftBank (TYO:9984) shares jumped more than 6%, while Advantest (TYO:6857) surged nearly 10%.
Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, on Monday disclosed rapid revenue growth alongside steep losses in its IPO filing, highlighting both the commercial potential of generative AI and the substantial costs of developing advanced models.
The planned listing has refocused attention on the ability of AI companies to attract public-market investors despite concerns about profitability and heavy infrastructure spending.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 3% overnight, its biggest daily gain in more than a month, as investors returned to chipmakers and companies supplying AI infrastructure.
China and Hong Kong shares, however, lagged the broader regional rally. China's Shanghai Composite and the blue-chip Shanghai Shenzhen CSI 300 traded largely flat.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng index edged down 0.3%, but major chipmakers SMIC (HK:0981) and Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor (HK:1347) rose modestly.
Major tech earnings, central bank meetings loom
Elsewhere, Singapore's Straits Times Index ticked 0.1% lower, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 0.2%.
Futures tied to India's Nifty 50 gained 0.1%.
Investors prepare for results from major technology companies, including Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOGL), Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) and Amazon Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN), later this week.
Their earnings and capital expenditure plans are expected to provide crucial evidence of whether spending on data centres, semiconductors and computing infrastructure is generating sufficient revenue and profits to justify lofty valuations.
The AI rally has faced pressure in October as investors questioned the sustainability of the investment boom, particularly as borrowing costs remain elevated.
Investors are also bracing for monetary policy decisions from the U.S. Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of Japan.
All three are widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, shifting attention to policymakers' comments for clues about the future path of borrowing costs.
Oil prices and geopolitical risks remain another source of uncertainty. Crude extended losses on Tuesday from near six-month highs as diplomatic efforts raised hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East, although attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure kept concerns about supply disruptions alive.
Persistently high energy prices could fuel inflation and complicate the outlook for central banks, potentially limiting the scope for monetary easing.

title: Oil extends losses as Iran mediation efforts ease escalation fears
full_text:
Investing.com-- Oil prices edged lower in Asian trading on Tuesday, falling for a second straight session as diplomatic efforts to ease the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran tempered fears of a broader regional escalation.
As of 20:10 ET (00:10 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in December fell 0.6% to $115.15 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 0.5% to $105.25 per barrel.
The retreat followed a rally last week that pushed Brent crude futures to six-month highs, driven by fears of further attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Middle East.
Get premium commodity market insights with InvestingPro subscription
The latest diplomatic push has focused on talks involving Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, while Qatari officials have also been engaging with Tehran in efforts to prevent the conflict from widening.
Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian leaders in Tehran on Monday, seeking to reduce regional tensions and open channels for negotiations.
Discussions included Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, the possibility of U.S.-Iran talks, disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Washington's blockade of Iranian ports, reports showed.
The diplomatic efforts have helped ease some of the immediate concerns about further military escalation, but investors remain cautious about whether they will produce a lasting de-escalation.
U.S. President Donald Trump has continued to leave open the possibility of further military action against Iran, while Tehran has said negotiations with Washington would require concessions, including an end to the U.S. blockade and the lifting of sanctions on Iranian oil exports.
The risks to supply remain substantial. The Iran conflict has disrupted commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, two important routes for global energy trade.
Houthi forces said on Monday they had attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pipeline and Riyadh airport, although Saudi Arabia had not immediately confirmed the claims. The kingdom has reported intercepting missiles and drones in recent days.
The International Energy Agency's executive director, Fatih Birol, said on Monday that energy markets were unlikely to return to their pre-war conditions in 2027, underscoring concerns about the lasting impact of the conflict on supply chains.
Saudi Aramco also plans to begin storing crude oil in Singapore in the second half of 2027, an initiative announced by Saudi and Singaporean energy ministers to strengthen the resilience of its regional supply chain.

title: Gold slips near $4,010 as traders await Fed decision, Iran diplomacy offers hope
full_text:
Investing.com -- Gold prices edged lower on Tuesday as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision this week, with diplomatic efforts to ease the U.S.-Iran conflict offering some relief to energy markets even as inflation concerns continued to weigh on bullion.
At 20:53 ET (00:53 GMT), XAU/USD fell 0.2% to $4,010.39 an ounce, while U.S. gold futures declined 0.3% to $4,023.57. XAG/USD was little changed at $53.9605 an ounce, while XPT/USD edged down 0.1% to $1,529.27. XPD/USD rose 0.1% to $1,046.65, while palladium futures fell 0.9% to $1,043.25. The U.S. Dollar Index rose marginally to 102.04.
Gold had gained 0.5% in the previous session before giving up ground as traders assessed the prospect of the Fed keeping rates unchanged at its meeting this week.
Oil prices fell for a second consecutive session as a fresh round of diplomatic efforts raised hopes of preventing a further escalation of the U.S.-Iran conflict. Meanwhile, stocks were poised to recover as enthusiasm for artificial intelligence investments returned following last week's selloff.
Despite the improved diplomatic outlook, gold remains under pressure from inflation concerns linked to persistently high energy prices.
Markets are pricing in roughly a 10% probability of an interest-rate increase at the Fed's meeting this week, although elevated energy prices continue to fuel expectations of a hike before the end of the year.
Traders initially increased their bets on an October rate hike after hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation data, but comments from central bank officials subsequently tempered those expectations.
Investors will watch the Fed's decision on Wednesday for clues on the policy outlook, while developments in U.S.-Iran diplomacy and energy prices remain important influences on inflation expectations.
A further easing in geopolitical tensions could help contain energy costs, but persistent inflation could keep the prospect of additional monetary tightening in focus.

title: SK Hynix shares rise to two-week high on report of $12 billion dividend
full_text:
Investing.com -- SK Hynix shares rose to a two-week high on Tuesday after South Korean newspaper Dong-A Ilbo reported that the memory chipmaker was considering a special dividend of about 16 trillion won ($12 billion), ahead of its third-quarter earnings announcement on Wednesday.
SK Hynix shares climbed 7.14% to 1,366,000 won, touching their highest level since October 14 and outperforming the broader KOSPI, which rose 3.81% in morning trading.
Dong-A Ilbo reported on Monday that the proposed special dividend could be funded by gains from SK Hynix's sale of its stake in Japanese memory chipmaker Kioxia. SK Hynix invested about 4 trillion won in Kioxia in 2018 through a Bain Capital-led consortium of US, Japanese and South Korean investors.
However, SK Hynix has not confirmed the reported dividend. In a regulatory filing on Monday, the company said it was reviewing various shareholder return measures to enhance shareholder value, but that no decisions had been made as of the filing date.
It said additional measures would be announced alongside its third-quarter results on Wednesday, subject to board approval.
The potential payout comes as investors press major memory chipmakers to return more cash following strong profits driven by demand for high-bandwidth memory and other chips used in artificial intelligence infrastructure.
In August, SK Hynix announced plans to buy back and cancel 40 trillion won worth of its own shares and allocate more than 50% of free cash flow generated between 2025 and 2027 to shareholder returns. The company also recently paused plans for a US listing of its Solidigm chip unit, citing market volatility.

title: Asian currencies mixed as dollar holds firm, yen retreats ahead of Fed decision
full_text:
The U.S. dollar index rose 0.09% to 102.05, while the USD/JPY pair gained 0.13% to 157.70, extending the yen's decline after it had strengthened last week on jitters over artificial-intelligence stocks. The USD/IDR pair rose 0.19% to 18,129.1, leaving the rupiah close to its weakest levels on record.
The yen was among the strongest-performing major currencies last week as concerns over AI-related equity valuations prompted investors to seek safer assets. That demand has since eased, leaving the currency vulnerable ahead of a busy week of central-bank decisions that could reshape the global interest-rate outlook.
Yen retreats as BOJ prepares to hold rates
The yen was last reported 0.2% weaker at 157.73 per dollar, further retreating from a one-month high reached last week. The USD/JPY pair was around 157.70.
The Bank of Japan is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% at its two-day meeting concluding Friday, while signaling that further increases remain possible as inflation pressures build.
The BOJ meeting follows the Federal Reserve's policy decision, due Wednesday, with the U.S. central bank expected to leave rates unchanged at its two-day meeting. Four other major central banks are also scheduled to announce policy decisions this week.
Rupiah near record lows as BI weighs stronger measures
The USD/IDR pair rose 0.2% to 18,129.1, extending pressure on the rupiah after the currency fell 0.4% on Monday and approached the historic low recorded in early June. The rupiah has lost around 8% against the dollar this year, putting it alongside the Philippine peso among Asia's weakest performers.
Elevated global bond yields, higher oil prices and concerns that Indonesia could lose its emerging-market classification under MSCI have contributed to foreign outflows and renewed selling pressure on the currency. MSCI's proposed reclassification has also raised concerns about reduced foreign investment in Indonesian equities, adding to the challenges facing the rupiah.
Bank Indonesia pledged last week to make “necessary adjustments” to its policy tools to maintain rupiah stability. It kept its benchmark rate at 5.75%, opting for currency intervention and stronger hedging incentives rather than a benchmark-rate increase that could weigh on the domestic economy.
The central bank also raised its deposit facility rate to 5.00% from 4.75%, while strengthening incentives aimed at attracting foreign capital and supporting the rupiah.
Other Asian currencies trade mixed
The Chinese yuan was steady, with the USD/CNH pair around 6.6678, while the USD/CNY pair fell 0.03% to 6.6683. The South Korean won strengthened modestly, with the USD/KRW pair down 0.1% at 1,324.36.
The Australian dollar rose 0.1% to $0.7025, while the New Zealand dollar gained 0.3% to $0.5695. Elsewhere, the USD/INR pair rose 0.2% to 95.353, indicating a weaker rupee, while the USD/SGD pair gained 0.04% to 1.2809.
The EUR/USD pair slipped 0.02% to 1.1172, while the GBP/USD pair was unchanged at 1.3342.
The currency markets remain focused on this week's central-bank decisions, with the Fed's expected pause and the BOJ's guidance likely to influence the dollar-yen pair, while continued foreign outflows leave the rupiah especially vulnerable to further pressure.

title: U.S. stock futures rise as Anthropic IPO buzz boosts tech; Fed, earnings on tap
full_text:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures rose slightly on Monday evening, with technology stocks remaining upbeat after Anthropic’s filing for an initial public offering helped spur some gains in the battered sector.
Focus remained squarely on a host of major tech earnings, as well as a Federal Reserve meeting due later in the week.
S&P 500 Futures rose 0.05% to 29,495.25 points by 19:33 ET (23:33 GMT). Nasdaq 100 Futures rose 0.21% to 29,498.50 points, while Dow Jones Futures fell 0.03% to 52,533.0 points.
Get more insights on Wall St and the biggest tech stocks by subscribing to InvestingPro
Anthropic IPO buzz helps stem tech losses
Futures firmed after a positive session on Wall Street, where stock indexes recovered a measure of recent losses on a recovery in tech.
The S&P 500 rose 0.7%, the NASDAQ Composite added 0.8%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.28% on Monday.
The AI trade remained in focus Anthropic filed for an IPO earlier on Monday, with the filing further underscoring the artificial intelligence startup’s ambitious plans for growth.
But the filing also highlighted the steep costs associated with developing and scaling up advanced AI models– the company’s net loss in the first half of 2026 surged fivefold to about $80.7 billion, while revenue stood at about $16.3 billion.
The company, which plans to trade under the ticker ANT, is reportedly being valued at around $1.5 trillion, down from earlier projections of $2 trillion.
Its plans for a public listing also come amid heightened scrutiny towards AI-related stocks, as investors increasingly questioned whether the debt-fueled spending in the sector would be able to yield adequate returns.
Said questions had battered AI and tech valuations over the past two weeks, also sparking deep losses on Wall Street.
A host of megacap tech earnings are expected to provide more cues on the AI trade this week. Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) and Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) will report September quarter earnings on Wednesday, followed by Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) on Thursday.
Memory chip maker Seagate Technology PLC (NASDAQ:STX) is set to report on Tuesday, as are plane maker Boeing Co (NYSE:BA) and copper giant Freeport-McMoRan Inc (NYSE:FCX).
Fed meeting on tap; hold largely expected
The Fed is also set to kick off a two-day meeting on Tuesday, and is broadly expected to leave rates unchanged at its conclusion on Wednesday.
The central bank is expected to wait and see the effects of a 25 basis point rate hike in September– its first such move since 2023, which brought rates to 4.0%.
Comments from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will be closely scrutinized for more insight on the central bank’s plans to raise rates further. Warsh had struck a hawkish chord in September, warning that sticky inflation was likely to invite more hikes.
Beyond the Fed, focus this week is also on third-quarter gross domestic product data, and PCE price index data– the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge. Both prints are due on Thursday.

title: China’s industrial profit growth picks up amid deepening economic divergence
full_text:
BEIJING, Oct 27 (Reuters) - China’s industrial profits grew at a faster pace in September, though a deepening divergence across the economy weighed on business earnings.
Profits at industrial firms rose 14.4% from a year earlier last month, quickening from a 4.2% increase in August, data from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showed on Tuesday. Profits were up 15.5% in the first nine months of this year, largely unchanged from the 15.7% increase in the January-August period.
The sectoral divide remained pronounced, with profits in the computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing category more than doubling over the nine-month period, whereas profits in the furniture manufacturing sector fell by more than half, making it one of the worst performers.
Also casting a shadow over the sustainability of profit growth, export-oriented firms are bracing for greater uncertainty as expanding trade surpluses stoke tensions with trading partners, particularly Europe.
However, CITIC Bank International’s chief China economist, Ding Meng, expressed optimism about the outlook because of the rapid growth in AI-related industries.
"This suggests that domestic and external demand generated by the development of the AI supply chain has become a key force supporting industrial profits," he said.
"Barring a major reversal in the global AI investment boom, industrial profits are expected to continue growing at a rapid pace."
A stronger-than-expected 4.5% expansion in third-quarter GDP put China within reach of its annual growth target of 4.5% to 5.0%, but disparities across different parts of the economy suggest the recovery remains unbalanced, with persistent weakness in some sectors continuing to erode corporate profitability.
That pressure has become increasingly visible at the company level. Net profit growth at the world’s largest electric vehicle battery maker, CATL, slowed sharply in the past quarter, as intense competition in the EV battery market squeezed margins at a time when China’s auto sales were in a downturn.
China will continue to leverage macroeconomic policies to support growth, expand domestic demand and optimize supply, said NBS statistician Yu Weining, underscoring a push to replace traditional growth drivers with new ones.
Industrial profit figures cover firms with yearly revenue of at least 20 million yuan ($3.0 million) from main operations.
($1 = 6.6702 Chinese yuan)

title: Japan’s GMO Internet warns users of impending ransomware attack
full_text:

title: Judge extends block on Trump plans to renovate Washington golf course
full_text:
By Kanishka Singh
WASHINGTON, Oct 26 (Reuters) - A US judge extended on Monday a court order blocking President Donald Trump’s plans to renovate a historic Washington golf course where she had deemed a removal of trees "inexcusable".
The renovation, at the center of a lawsuit over environmental and historic preservation concerns, is one of the projects Trump is pursuing to reshape landmarks in the US capital.
"The court still does not speak for the trees," US District Judge Ana Reyes said in her order filed in the district court for the District of Columbia, adding, "It speaks only for the rule of law."
Her order barred the government from "removing or damaging additional trees" on the course.
It also ordered the government to provide 10 business days’ of written advance notice before it makes any "irreparable modification" at the park, pending the suit outcome.
Two weeks earlier, Reyes faulted the conduct of Justice Department lawyers in the lawsuit seeking to halt the Trump administration’s takeover of the historic golf course.
It was "inexcusable" that hundreds of trees were removed from the course during the prior weekend, she added.
Last week Trump said his administration would begin renovation work immediately, despite the judge’s order that work could not proceed without prior notice to the court.
In an online post, Trump declared his administration had "an absolute right" to proceed, while blasting the judge as "lunatic," and calling the lawsuit "ridiculous."
The DC Preservation League sued in February to halt the takeover, on the grounds that it would violate environmental laws and "irreparably destroy a priceless piece of American history."
Reyes said the government had asked her to disregard Trump’s statements about the renovation plans.
"Rarely, if ever, has the United States Department of Justice urged a federal court not to believe the sitting president," Reyes said.
"This started as a case about golf ... But it has become much more," she added.
"It now forces the court to reconcile assertions by President Donald J. Trump with the sworn testimony of multiple government employees and the argument of senior DOJ attorneys."

title: Ex-BOJ chief Kuroda backs more rate hikes, his former deputy urges caution
full_text:
By Leika Kihara
TOKYO, Oct 27 (Reuters) - The Bank of Japan will likely consider raising interest rates at each upcoming meeting, according to a new book by former bank chief Haruhiko Kuroda, who supported his successor’s current push to unwind a decade of extremely loose monetary policy.
Kuroda’s views contrast with those of his former deputy Masazumi Wakatabe, whose book published in September warned against premature rate hikes and urged policymakers to stay focused on boosting demand.
The remarks show a divergence in policy thinking between Kuroda, who took part in the monetary leg of former premier Shinzo Abe’s "Abenomics" reflationist policies, and Wakatabe who, together with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, focuses on preserving the legacies of Abenomics.
While raising interest rates too hastily could cause economic stagnation, moving too slowly could prevent incumbent governor Kazuo Ueda from completing policy normalisation, Kuroda said.
"I’m sure the BOJ will examine whether to raise interest rates by 25 basis point at each policy meeting to bring them close to levels deemed neutral to the economy," he said in the book published this month, which looked back at his decade at the helm at the BOJ.
Wakatabe, however, believes there are other priorities currently for monetary policy.
"Real economic growth remains low and while Japan is experiencing inflation, half of the price rises are driven by cost-push factors," Wakatabe said in his book, published in September, on Takaichi’s economic policies.
Wakatabe is known as a reflationist with close ties to Takaichi and currently serves as a member of a key government economic panel.
WAKATABE URGES CAUTION
Kuroda deployed a radical stimulus programme in 2013 with a pledge to fire up inflation to the BOJ’s 2% target in two years. But the target proved elusive, forcing the BOJ to maintain ultra-loose policy throughout his term that ended in 2023.
Ueda steered an exit from Kuroda’s stimulus in 2024, as a tight job market and rising raw material costs from the Ukraine war lifted consumer inflation.
The BOJ has raised rates several times, including in September to a 31-year high of 1.25%, and is expected to declare victory on Friday in its 14-year battle to meet its price target.
In his book, Kuroda said he sought to eradicate Japan’s deflationary mindset with simple communication, and "cut off his escape route" by setting a timeframe for hitting the price goal at the risk of depriving the BOJ of policy flexibility.
He said he became convinced Japan had fully emerged from deflation around 2024 as wages began to rise.
Wakatabe served as deputy BOJ governor from 2018 to 2023. He is seen as among candidates to succeed Ueda when his term ends in 2028, if Takaichi were to stay on as premier long enough to hand-pick the next BOJ chief.
"The BOJ would need to do quite some explaining if it were to raise rates when real economic growth is negative and price rises are driven mostly by cost-push factors," Wakatabe wrote in his book.
A rate hike may become possible if Takaichi’s spending plans and growth strategies stimulate investment and fund demand, thereby pushing up Japan’s neutral rate, he said.

title: China industrial profits rise 14.4% in September on AI demand
full_text:
Investing.com -- Chinese industrial profits grew in September, aided chiefly by the artificial intelligence sector, while consumer-oriented sectors continued to lag amid sluggish demand.
Industrial profits grew 14.4% in September compared to the same month last year, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics released Tuesday.
The September figure marked the fastest growth rate since June.
For the first nine months of 2026, industrial profits at large firms increased 15.5%, a slight decline from the 15.7% growth recorded in the January-September period.
Industrial earnings shifted to double-digit growth rates earlier in 2026 after posting modest gains in 2025. The sector had contracted for three consecutive years before last year’s recovery.

title: Porsche profit rebounds in nine-month period after restructuring costs
full_text:
BERLIN, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Volkswagen’s embattled sports car maker Porsche on Tuesday reported a recovery in profit in the first nine months of the year, an early test of CEO Michael Leiters’ turnaround plan to downsize and retreat from China.
Operating profit of €1.74 billion ($1.94 billion) followed a weak prior-year result of €40 million, when the carmaker was hit by €2.7 billion in costs largely related to its halted electrification strategy, the company said.
"Even in a challenging market environment, Porsche is showing itself to be financially robust," Porsche finance chief Jochen Breckner said, confirming the carmaker’s guidance for 2026.
Leiters was brought in at the start of the year to correct Porsche’s course. He plans to restore profitability with more customisation and exclusive higher-margin models.
Declining sales in China have hit Porsche as well as parent Volkswagen and fellow subsidiary Audi, prompting a sweeping restructuring of the group.
Porsche’s operating return on sales hit a record low of 1.1% in 2025 but improved to 6.9% in the nine-month period, within a targeted range of 5.5% to 7.5% for the full year.

title: HSBC shares hit 20-week low as profit misses estimates; announces $1bn buyback
full_text:
Investing.com -- HSBC Holdings shares fell to a nearly 20-week low on Tuesday, as investors looked past stronger quarterly earnings and a fresh share-buyback plan from Europe’s largest bank.
The stock fell 4.29% to HK$136.10, after touching an intraday low of HK$134.70, its lowest level since June 11. The decline underperformed the broader Hang Seng Index, which was down 0.48% in afternoon trading.
Get InvestingPro and stay ahead of stock and FX market moves-- with 55% off for a limited period
HSBC said it plans to launch an additional share buyback of up to $1 billion after reporting higher third-quarter profit, supported by stronger net interest income and lower credit impairment charges. The bank expects to complete the buyback by the announcement of its full-year 2026 results.
Pretax profit rose 32% year on year to $9.63 billion in the July-September quarter from $7.30 billion a year earlier, but fell short of Bloomberg estimates of $9.7 billion.
The bank’s annualised return on average tangible equity (RoTE) improved to 17.7% from 12.3% a year earlier, while its cost-efficiency ratio narrowed to 47.4% from 56.6%. Net interest margin remained stable at 1.57%, while its common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio fell to 13.9% from 14.1% at the end of June.
Revenue increased 5% year on year to $18.62 billion, primarily reflecting growth in banking net interest income. Net interest income rose 6% to $9.31 billion, supported by deposit growth and reinvestment of the bank’s structural hedge at higher yields.
Credit impairment charges declined 17% to $832 million, primarily reflecting lower charges related to Hong Kong commercial real estate exposures, alongside reduced charges in the UK and Mexico. Profit after tax climbed 38% to $7.57 billion.
HSBC maintained its target for RoTE of 17% or better in 2026, 2027 and 2028, excluding notable items. It also reiterated its expectation for 2026 banking net interest income of at least $46 billion and operating expense growth of approximately 1% on a target basis.
The bank’s board approved a third interim dividend of $0.10 per ordinary share, alongside the planned buyback.

title: BCA cuts Brazil stock rating on Lula win, fiscal concerns
full_text:
Investing.com - BCA downgraded its stock rating on Brazilian equities following President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s election victory, citing concerns over fiscal policy and structural reform prospects.
The firm reduced its exposure to Brazilian stocks relative to the emerging markets benchmark despite Monday’s selloff.
Lula’s election triggered a sharp decline in Brazilian financial assets. The real fell roughly 9%, and the IBOVESPA declined over 13%, representing a major common currency stock market decline.
BCA expects Brazilian markets to follow a vicious cycle in the coming weeks. Default rates among consumers and businesses are rising despite persistent fiscal stimulus. If fiscal stimulus is curbed to quell market concerns, the economy will be plunged into recession.
The falling currency will drive imported inflation higher, necessitating rate hikes until the economy slows. BCA stated that equities are likely the most vulnerable asset class in Brazil and described Brazilian stocks as a value trap despite the potential for a near-term bounce.
The firm also recommended reducing cyclical exposure to Brazilian debt, including sovereign and domestic bonds. BCA noted there is no guarantee Lula will act to quell markets or that markets will respond in the near term, and no politically feasible path to containing the debt exists even if the right-leaning Congress contains Lula’s fiscal measures.

title: Assa Abloy posts record sales, profit and margin in third quarter
full_text:
Investing.com -- Assa Abloy reported record third-quarter results Tuesday, with sales broadly in line with analyst estimates. Sales rose 7% to 40.77 billion Swedish crowns, compared to the IBES estimate of 40.75 billion crowns. Organic growth stood at 4%, acquisitions added 2%, and currency added 1%.
Operating income before amortization (EBITA) rose 12% to 7.61 billion crowns, and the margin widened to 18.7% from 17.9%. Operating income (EBIT) rose 11% to 7.10 billion crowns, with a margin of 17.4%, up from 16.8%.
Net income rose 14% to 4.72 billion crowns, and earnings per share rose 14% to 4.24 crowns. Operating cash flow rose 6% to 7.41 billion crowns, a cash conversion rate of 117%.
Chief Executive Nico Delvaux said the lock maker’s margin improved on "excellent operating leverage" of 47% from price realization and cost efficiencies. It was the seventh consecutive quarter of organic sales growth despite geopolitical and economic uncertainty.
Regionally, organic sales rose 6% in the Americas and 5% in Europe, the Middle East, India and Africa, with non-residential strength in the Americas and very strong growth in Central Europe. Asia Pacific declined 1%, on weak sales in Greater China.
Global Technologies grew 4%, led by its HID unit, while Entrance Systems grew 3%.
For the first nine months, sales rose 1% to 115.8 billion crowns, with organic growth of 3%, and operating income rose 6% to 19.2 billion crowns. Delvaux said he is confident of delivering another strong year.
The company plans to launch its 11th manufacturing footprint program in the fourth quarter.

title: Porsche keeps 2026 outlook as Q3 profit rebounds, deliveries fall 16%
full_text:
Investing.com -- Porsche confirmed its 2026 outlook on Tuesday as a sharp rebound in nine-month operating profit came largely from lower restructuring costs, with deliveries down 16% and third-quarter cash flow propped up by the sale of its Bugatti Rimac stake.
The company kept its full-year forecast for group sales revenue of €35 billion to €36 billion, an operating return on sales of 5.5% to 7.5% and an automotive net cash flow margin of 5.5% to 7.5%.
It also expects an automotive EBITDA margin of 15% to 17% and a battery-electric share of deliveries of 24% to 26%. The cash flow margin guidance was raised in September after the Bugatti Rimac sale.
Operating profit at the Stuttgart-based sports car maker was €1.74 billion in the first nine months, up from €40 million a year earlier, and operating return on sales was 6.9% versus 0.2%.
Restructuring costs were about €500 million, compared with €2.7 billion in the same period last year.
Sales revenue fell to €25.28 billion from €26.86 billion a year earlier, a smaller drop than deliveries, which fell to 178,532 vehicles from 212,509.
Porsche said it is sticking to its "Value over Volume" approach in China, where the market remains challenging.
Automotive net cash flow rose to €2.50 billion from €1.34 billion a year earlier, mainly because of cash received from the sale of Porsche’s shares in Bugatti Rimac and the Rimac Group, which was completed in the third quarter.
The sale produced a gain of €593 million, and the group received €984 million in cash, most of it counted in automotive net cash flow.
Three one-off items cut third-quarter automotive net cash flow: between €100 million and €200 million linked to the restructuring, €250 million for further funding of pension obligations and €200 million in charges from U.S. tariffs. The automotive net cash flow margin was 11.3% for the nine months versus 5.6% a year earlier.
Net liquidity in the automotive business rose by €884 million to €8.23 billion at Sept. 30 from the end of 2025, mainly because of cash generated by the automotive business.
Automotive EBITDA margin was 17.3%, versus 11.9% a year earlier. Battery-electric vehicles made up 21.7% of deliveries versus 23.1% a year earlier, as the prior-year figure was lifted by strong sales of the all-electric Macan in 2025.

title: Caviar, champagne and a Porsche ride as aviation widens its class divide
full_text:
By Alessandro Parodi and Joanna Plucinska
ROISSY-EN-FRANCE, France, Oct 27 (Reuters) - A sleek black Porsche Cayenne glides across the tarmac at Charles de Gaulle airport in Paris as it delivers the elite passengers many airlines are seeking to court to an Air France Boeing 777 jet.
The sharpened focus on the world’s wealthiest is an industry reaction to a surge in fuel prices that has squeezed margins and led to fare increases that have deterred the more cost-conscious economy passengers.
Air France, which says its "La Première", or first-class, fares rank among the industry’s most expensive, is seeking to stand apart by spending €1 billion ($1 billion) on upgrading its services.
In addition to the private car to the plane, Première class customers get their own entrance at the airport, discrete security checks, a lounge with a spa and caviar and champagne while they wait.
On board, they can spend their flight in a private suite, wearing designer pyjamas and eating food designed by Michelin-star chefs.
"We really wanted to move upmarket," Air France’s Executive Vice President Customer Fabien Pelous told Reuters on board the plane.
"Over the past five years, we have created this new cabin and we have paid attention to every detail to push it to the maximum of the expectations of our customers," Pelous said. "We wanted to create the space like in a private jet."
Apart from the €1 billion investment in lounges, cabins and improved WiFi over a five-year period, he said Air France was spending another €1 billion a year as part on its annual fleet renewal costs.
SOCIETY’S WIDENING DIVIDE
The widening gap between the experience of elite airline passengers and those flying economy reflects society as a whole.
The surge in fuel costs, linked to the US-Israeli war with Iran, and an attendant rise in inflation has helped to spark social unrest over the cost of living in some countries, including France. It coincides with an artificial intelligence-led surge in stock markets and the creation of a new super-rich class.
Aviation analyst John Strickland said airlines were willing to reduce the overall number of seats in order to increase their premium sector, which he said had grown substantially.
"It’s understandable why airlines are investing in that, changing their cabin configurations with lower overall seats," he said.
Industry body the International Air Transport Association in a report in June found that overall growth in travel was slowing, with passenger traffic, across all classes, expected to increase by only 2.1% this year, compared with 5.3% last year.
Air France does not break out separate figures for its highest class, but said the combined first and business-class sector grew by 28.1% in 2025 and 26.9% in 2024, while economy revenue stagnated.
Its first-class flights start at just below $14,000 for a Paris-New York return ticket, which the company says offers a unique experience.
"We did invest a lot of money both on the ground and in the air," Chief Executive Ben Smith told Reuters in an interview. "This particular cabin or class is unmatched."
The Skytrax World Airline Awards, one of the best-known airline rankings, this year named Air France the world’s best first-class airline.
THE ADVANTAGE OF ANONYMITY
The amount of space and resources allocated to each first-class passenger means they have a heavy carbon footprint, although lighter than if they travelled in a private jet.
Air France says its services can also be preferable for showbiz stars and other VIP travellers because they provide anonymity whereas private jets, which owners have to register, can be tracked on aviation surveillance websites.
Other airlines are also seeking to increase their luxury appeal.
In Asia, Air India has rolled out new cabins on some international routes, while IAG-owned British Airways earlier this month said it was revamping its A380 fleet to reduce the overall number of seats and increase the focus on premium customers.
Roberto Alvo, the chief executive of LATAM Airlines Group, said this month he believed airlines with robust premium offerings would emerge the strongest from the current economic turmoil, which he predicted would lead to some consolidation.
In the US, traditionally low-fare airlines such as Southwest, Frontier, JetBlue and Allegiant are moving upmarket.
Delta Air Lines has also said it is targeting the upper end of what is known as a "K-shaped economy", in which sections of the population are becoming richer and others — the downward arm of the K — are becoming poorer.
Air France’s Pelous acknowledged that even some of the rich could start to worry more about cost as the war in Iran, which began at the end of February, continues to drive energy prices, but he said the company would not change its luxury strategy.
The price of jet fuel, which accounts for 30% to 40% of airlines’ expenses, has more than doubled since the start of the year.
"The first impact of this war is a huge increase in the cost of petrol that definitely affects us," Pelous said. "But despite this complicated context, we want to maintain our strategy to move upmarket."
($1 = 0.8905 euros)

title: Analysis-US airlines favor higher fares over fuller planes as fuel costs squeeze profits
full_text:
By Rajesh Kumar Singh
CHICAGO, Oct 23 (Reuters) - US airlines are increasingly willing to fly with empty seats rather than slash fares simply to fill them, betting that disciplined pricing and flight schedules will help protect profits at a time of soaring fuel costs.
The strategy has delivered substantial revenue gains as demand has held up despite sharp fare increases. Yet profits have still been squeezed as jet fuel prices surged roughly 90% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in February, forcing several major carriers to cut earnings forecasts.
Executives at Delta Air Lines, United Airlines, American Airlines, Southwest Airlines and Alaska Air Group have emphasized protecting margins over boosting passenger volumes.
Their resolve faces a test in 2027. Industry schedules point to more flying capacity, potentially intensifying competition for passengers even as fuel prices are expected to stay high and making this year’s substantial fare gains harder to repeat.
"If fuel stays elevated, we have to continue to push yield up so that we can make a bit of money," American Chief Financial Officer Devon May told Reuters on Thursday. Yield is the revenue airlines collect for each mile passengers fly.
Six major US airlines plan to grow domestic capacity 3.0% in the fourth quarter from a year earlier and 3.8% in the first quarter of 2027, a sharp acceleration from just 0.2% growth in the third quarter, according to Airlines for America, citing Cirium data.
US air fares rose an average of nearly 23% year-on-year in the seven months through September, far outpacing the 3.6% average increase in overall consumer prices, according to Labor Department data.
Airlines are still seeking increases. JetBlue Airways initiated a $10 one-way increase in domestic published fares on Wednesday, JP Morgan said, following a similar United-led increase the previous week that Southwest subsequently matched.
United said it had nothing further to add, while Southwest said it does not publicly discuss pricing. JetBlue did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
A DIFFERENT APPROACH
Airlines have long balanced fares against how full their planes are. But elevated fuel costs have made executives more willing to sacrifice occupancy and avoid discounts.
United’s commercial chief Andrew Nocella offered an example during Wednesday’s earnings call. Its leisure load factor, a measure of how many available seats are occupied, fell 1.3 percentage points in the third quarter.
Nocella acknowledged that the decline showed "a small amount of elasticity given higher ticket prices," but called it "a trade we would make every day."
American Airlines planes flew less full in the third quarter even as passenger yields jumped more than 18%. Finance chief May told Reuters the trade was deliberate.
Delta has also been "managing the business for margins," CEO Ed Bastian said.
Across Delta, United, American, Southwest and Alaska, passenger revenue rose nearly $8.8 billion, or 18%, in the third quarter from a year earlier, while passenger traffic increased less than 1%.
The divergence shows how much revenue growth now depends on earning more from each passenger rather than carrying more of them. Premium products and changes in passenger mix have also contributed to the gains.
The Transportation Security Administration screened 2.9% fewer people at US airports in the quarter than a year earlier, raising questions about whether higher fares are beginning to discourage travel. Limited capacity growth and the shutdown of budget carrier Spirit Airlines have also weighed on traffic.
Airline executives insisted that demand remains resilient.
"Those higher fares are not causing an erosion of volumes," Southwest CEO Bob Jordan told analysts, after the airline reported a nearly 22% increase in average passenger fares in the first nine months of this year.
THE 2027 TEST
But record revenues have not been enough to shield profits from soaring fuel costs. Gulf Coast spot jet fuel prices have risen from $2.43 a gallon before the war began in February to $4.63 on October 20, according to US Energy Information Administration data.
Delta and Southwest have cut their annual earnings forecasts, while American expects a full-year loss despite sharply higher passenger revenue.
Airlines are now scrutinizing expansion plans. American intends to slow growth considerably next year, with May saying the carrier was reassessing whether additional flights would generate enough revenue to cover their operating costs.
Southwest has pledged not to pursue growth at the expense of profitability, while United executives have cautioned that airlines’ published 2027 capacity plans may not materialize.
Such restraint could help maintain higher fares. But flying less can raise operating costs per seat, while pushing prices higher risks discouraging travelers who have already absorbed steep increases.
But airline executives say a disciplined approach on capacity can allow the industry to hold on to pricing gains.
"We think these yield gains are very sustainable," May said.

title: Oil rises slightly as diplomacy hopes counter renewed Houthi attacks
full_text:
By Sethuraman N R
NEW DELHI, Oct 27 (Reuters) - Oil prices turned positive on Tuesday after a fall of about 1%, earlier in the session, as the chance of talks in Tehran eased fears of a broader Middle East supply shock, while renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia highlighted persistent risks.
Brent crude futures was up 40 cents, or 0.4%, at $116.24 a barrel by 0718 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was up 30 cents, or 0.3%, at $102.07. Both fell 1% earlier in the session.
Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday aimed at easing tension in the Middle East.
The four countries agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation in peace and security, Iranian state media said.
"Prices remain elevated amid persistent geopolitical uncertainties," said Sugandha Sachdeva, founder of SS WealthStreet, a New Delhi-based research firm, adding that some profit taking earlier in the session was fuelled by hopes of a breakthrough in talks between the US and Iran, she said.
Last week, Brent prices surged to more than $117 a barrel, the highest since April, after a wave of Iranian attacks on tankers around the Strait of Hormuz. Brent prices touched $117 on Monday as well.
Scope for peace looked fragile, however, with renewed attacks by Iran-aligned Houthis on key producer Saudi Arabia.
October has been the worst month for attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and nearby waterways, data from a Washington-based think tank shows, among worldwide maritime security incidents it has tracked since 2017.
The war rippling across the Middle East has brought into focus the narrow waterway of the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of global energy supplies before the conflict erupted in February.
The oil market is vulnerable with stress across areas such as supply, logistics, inventories and refining, ANZ Research said in a note.
Gulf crude exports fell for a fourth straight week and flows through the Strait of Hormuz were just about 60% of their normal level, while global distillate inventories held nearly 5% below their five-year average, it added.
